title: kitty,renderer: Add ref-counted images and eliminate unnecessary copies in the renderer
body:
# Reference counted types and a canonical image type
This PR, builds on #13285, and adds the Image (canonical image data + format and size metadata) and ArcImage (shared ref-counted) types to unify image types in `kitty/graphics_storage.zig` (wrapping Image with kitty graphics protocol details) and `renderer/image.zig` (wrapping Image with renderer upload state). A type utility is used to make `AtomicRefCounted(T). I thought through this work this based on my understanding of Rust's Arc<T> type.

>*Edited to rename CpuImage to Image and explain other image types built on it. 

# Optimising away copies and conversions
This allows the renderer to increment a reference-count to image data for pending GPU upload immutable and valid.
Additionally, this PR lets the GraphicsAPI implementation decide which data formats are natively supported for uploads (OpenGL can upload RGB data into RGBA formats) to eliminate extra copies/swizzles.
On top, we defer CPU-side format conversion from reading terminal state to uploading the pending CPU image to the GPU so that cancelled uploads don't pay for format conversion and slow the renderer.

# Kitty Eviction Behaviour
~~This adds an explicit image_allocator field used for allocating Image.data slices and the control blocks for ArcImages, a followup could be to add verification of the eviction based on this allocator.~~

>*Edited to add the above paragraph
>**Edited, we removed the explicit image allocator for an unmanaged style

This changes the semantics of Kitty storage eviction to just drop the shared reference which may have its allocation kept alive by a clone of the shared reference. Overall, I think this is acceptable we can consider clones to "overcount" the allocated memory as the pessimistic memory usage when sharing cannot be done.

# Mutability for Animation Edits
Animation edits from the kitty protocol required mutable access, not sure if we had thread-safety bugs with in-place mutation there or locking kept us safe. But now the edit operations opportunistically convert a shared reference with ref-count = 1 into exclusive ownership for mutation and fallback to allocating new data.

# Benefits
Running `mpv --vo=kitty <video>` we can compare the `sudo perf record -s -p <ghostty process>` for renderer work done. The outputs are `perf report --stdio`

Mainly, we eliminate this line in the profile 
` 3.80%  renderer   ghostty   [.] wuffs_private_impl__swizzle_bgrw__bgr__x86_sse42`

> Now the renderer is mainly doing opengl calls and the swizzle has been elided
> Kitty image upload is now mostly memcopies in the io-reader and base64 decoding

# C API
I haven't changed the C API as it was mentioned as fine to break in the original PR, and I don't think I'm familiar enough with it to review LLM-generated code.

# AI Disclosure
Code was written by GPT 6 Astra and Sol, I iterated through designing the ArcCpuImage and CpuImage APIs based on the design I wanted and manually rewrote the comments created. I've read through the renderer and kitty code before for other PRs without LLM-assistance.
